requirements.quote:
frame:  The smallest unit of communication within an HTTP/2
      connection, consisting of a header and a variable-length sequence
      of octets structured according to the frame type.
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing an HTTP/2 frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat the frame as a header followed by a variable-length sequence of octets structured according to its frame type.
requirements.why_checkable: The component structure and frame-type-dependent payload encoding can be inspected in frame serialization and parsing.

requirements.quote:
HTTP/2 uses the "http" and "https" URI schemes defined in Section 4.2
   of [HTTP], with the same default port numbers as HTTP/1.1 [HTTP/1.1].
requirements.condition: When HTTP/2 is used with an HTTP URI.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the "http" and "https" URI schemes and the same default port numbers as HTTP/1.1.
requirements.why_checkable: URI-scheme acceptance and default-port selection are observable implementation behaviors.

requirements.quote:
The means by which support for HTTP/2 is determined is different for
   "http" and "https" URIs.  Discovery for "https" URIs is described in
   Section 3.2.  HTTP/2 support for "http" URIs can only be discovered
   by out-of-band means and requires prior knowledge of the support as
   described in Section 3.3.
requirements.condition: When establishing HTTP/2 for an "http" URI.
requirements.required_behavior: Use out-of-band discovery and have prior knowledge that the server supports HTTP/2.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not infer HTTP/2 support for an "http" URI without out-of-band information and prior knowledge.
requirements.why_checkable: A connection-establishment test can determine whether cleartext HTTP/2 is attempted without configured or otherwise obtained prior knowledge.

requirements.quote:
The protocol defined in this document has two identifiers.  Creating
   a connection based on either implies the use of the transport,
   framing, and message semantics described in this document.
requirements.condition: When a connection is created based on either HTTP/2 protocol identifier.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the transport, framing, and message semantics defined for HTTP/2.
requirements.why_checkable: The negotiated identifier and the subsequent wire protocol can be compared for consistency.

requirements.quote:
*  The string "h2" identifies the protocol where HTTP/2 uses
      Transport Layer Security (TLS); see Section 9.2.  This identifier
      is used in the TLS Application-Layer Protocol Negotiation (ALPN)
      extension [TLS-ALPN] field and in any place where HTTP/2 over TLS
      is identified.
requirements.condition: When identifying HTTP/2 over TLS, including in ALPN.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the protocol identifier "h2".
requirements.why_checkable: The identifier placed in ALPN or another HTTP/2-over-TLS identification field is directly observable.

requirements.quote:
The "h2" string is serialized into an ALPN protocol identifier as
      the two-octet sequence: 0x68, 0x32.
requirements.condition: When serializing "h2" as an ALPN protocol identifier.
requirements.required_behavior: Serialize it as exactly the two octets 0x68, 0x32.
requirements.why_checkable: The serialized ALPN identifier has an exact length and byte sequence that can be compared on the wire.

requirements.quote:
*  The "h2c" string was previously used as a token for use in the
      HTTP Upgrade mechanism's Upgrade header field (Section 7.8 of
      [HTTP]).  This usage was never widely deployed and is deprecated
      by this document.  The same applies to the HTTP2-Settings header
      field, which was used with the upgrade to "h2c".
requirements.condition: When considering the HTTP Upgrade mechanism for HTTP/2.
requirements.why_checkable: The passage marks use of "h2c" and HTTP2-Settings for Upgrade as deprecated but does not state a precise required or forbidden implementation behavior.

requirements.quote:
A client that makes a request to an "https" URI uses TLS [TLS13] with
   the ALPN extension [TLS-ALPN].
requirements.condition: When a client makes a request to an "https" URI.
requirements.required_behavior: Use TLS with the ALPN extension.
requirements.why_checkable: TLS use and inclusion of ALPN are observable during connection establishment.

requirements.quote:
HTTP/2 over TLS uses the "h2" protocol identifier.  The "h2c"
   protocol identifier MUST NOT be sent by a client or selected by a
   server; the "h2c" protocol identifier describes a protocol that does
   not use TLS.
requirements.condition: When a client negotiates HTTP/2 over TLS.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the "h2" protocol identifier.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The client must not send the "h2c" protocol identifier.
requirements.why_checkable: The client's offered ALPN identifiers can be captured and checked.

requirements.quote:
HTTP/2 over TLS uses the "h2" protocol identifier.  The "h2c"
   protocol identifier MUST NOT be sent by a client or selected by a
   server; the "h2c" protocol identifier describes a protocol that does
   not use TLS.
requirements.condition: When a server negotiates HTTP/2 over TLS.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the "h2" protocol identifier.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The server must not select the "h2c" protocol identifier.
requirements.why_checkable: The server-selected ALPN identifier is observable during the TLS handshake.

requirements.quote:
Once TLS negotiation is complete, both the client and the server MUST
   send a connection preface (Section 3.4).
requirements.condition: Once TLS negotiation is complete.
requirements.required_behavior: The client must send its connection preface.
requirements.why_checkable: A trace can verify that the client sends a connection preface after completing TLS negotiation.

requirements.quote:
Once TLS negotiation is complete, both the client and the server MUST
   send a connection preface (Section 3.4).
requirements.condition: Once TLS negotiation is complete.
requirements.required_behavior: The server must send its connection preface.
requirements.why_checkable: A trace can verify that the server sends a connection preface after completing TLS negotiation.

requirements.quote:
A client that knows that a server supports HTTP/2 can establish a TCP
   connection and send the connection preface (Section 3.4) followed by
   HTTP/2 frames.  Servers can identify these connections by the
   presence of the connection preface.  This only affects the
   establishment of HTTP/2 connections over cleartext TCP; HTTP/2
   connections over TLS MUST use protocol negotiation in TLS [TLS-ALPN].
requirements.condition: When establishing an HTTP/2 connection over TLS.
requirements.required_behavior: Use protocol negotiation in TLS.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not establish HTTP/2 over TLS solely through the cleartext prior-knowledge procedure.
requirements.why_checkable: A TLS handshake can be inspected to verify use of protocol negotiation before HTTP/2 traffic.

requirements.quote:
A client that knows that a server supports HTTP/2 can establish a TCP
   connection and send the connection preface (Section 3.4) followed by
   HTTP/2 frames.  Servers can identify these connections by the
   presence of the connection preface.  This only affects the
   establishment of HTTP/2 connections over cleartext TCP; HTTP/2
   connections over TLS MUST use protocol negotiation in TLS [TLS-ALPN].
requirements.condition: When a client uses prior knowledge to establish HTTP/2 over cleartext TCP.
requirements.required_behavior: Send the client connection preface before subsequent HTTP/2 frames.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not send ordinary HTTP/2 frames before the connection preface.
requirements.why_checkable: The ordering of the preface and subsequent frames is directly observable in the TCP byte stream.

requirements.quote: Likewise, the server MUST send a connection preface (Section 3.4).
requirements.condition: When establishing HTTP/2 with prior knowledge.
requirements.required_behavior: The server must send a connection preface.
requirements.why_checkable: The server's initial HTTP/2 output can be inspected for its connection preface.

requirements.quote:
In HTTP/2, each endpoint is required to send a connection preface as
   a final confirmation of the protocol in use and to establish the
   initial settings for the HTTP/2 connection.  The client and server
   each send a different connection preface.
requirements.condition: When establishing an HTTP/2 connection.
requirements.required_behavior: Each endpoint must send its role-specific connection preface to confirm the protocol and establish initial settings.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The client and server must not use the same form of connection preface.
requirements.why_checkable: Traffic from both endpoints can be checked for the presence and role-specific form of each preface.

requirements.quote:
The client connection preface starts with a sequence of 24 octets,
   which in hex notation is:
requirements.condition: When sending the client connection preface.
requirements.required_behavior: Start the preface with a sequence of exactly 24 octets.
requirements.why_checkable: The initial sequence length can be counted directly from the connection bytes.

requirements.condition: When sending the initial 24-octet sequence of the client connection preface.
requirements.required_behavior: Send exactly the hexadecimal byte sequence 0x505249202a20485454502f322e300d0a0d0a534d0d0a0d0a.
requirements.why_checkable: The connection's first 24 octets can be compared byte-for-byte with the specified constant.

requirements.quote:
That is, the connection preface starts with the string "PRI *
   HTTP/2.0\r\n\r\nSM\r\n\r\n".  This sequence MUST be followed by a
   SETTINGS frame (Section 6.5), which MAY be empty.  The client sends
   the client connection preface as the first application data octets of
   a connection.
requirements.condition: When a client sends its connection preface.
requirements.required_behavior:
Start it with the string "PRI * HTTP/2.0

SM

".
requirements.why_checkable: The client's initial application bytes can be compared with the specified literal string.

requirements.quote:
That is, the connection preface starts with the string "PRI *
   HTTP/2.0\r\n\r\nSM\r\n\r\n".  This sequence MUST be followed by a
   SETTINGS frame (Section 6.5), which MAY be empty.  The client sends
   the client connection preface as the first application data octets of
   a connection.
requirements.condition: Immediately after the fixed 24-octet sequence in the client connection preface.
requirements.required_behavior: Send a SETTINGS frame next.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not place another frame or application data between the fixed sequence and the SETTINGS frame.
requirements.why_checkable: Frame order following the fixed preface sequence is visible in a connection trace.

requirements.quote:
That is, the connection preface starts with the string "PRI *
   HTTP/2.0\r\n\r\nSM\r\n\r\n".  This sequence MUST be followed by a
   SETTINGS frame (Section 6.5), which MAY be empty.  The client sends
   the client connection preface as the first application data octets of
   a connection.
requirements.condition: When sending the SETTINGS frame that follows the fixed client preface sequence.
requirements.required_behavior: Permit the SETTINGS frame to have an empty payload.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not reject or prevent this SETTINGS frame solely because its payload is empty.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can send or generate a zero-length SETTINGS payload and observe whether it is accepted.

requirements.quote:
That is, the connection preface starts with the string "PRI *
   HTTP/2.0\r\n\r\nSM\r\n\r\n".  This sequence MUST be followed by a
   SETTINGS frame (Section 6.5), which MAY be empty.  The client sends
   the client connection preface as the first application data octets of
   a connection.
requirements.condition: When a client begins sending application data on an HTTP/2 connection.
requirements.required_behavior: Send the client connection preface as the first application data octets.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not send other application data before the client connection preface.
requirements.why_checkable: The first application data octets on the connection can be captured and identified.

requirements.quote:
The server connection preface consists of a potentially empty
   SETTINGS frame (Section 6.5) that MUST be the first frame the server
   sends in the HTTP/2 connection.
requirements.condition: When a server sends its HTTP/2 connection preface.
requirements.required_behavior: The preface must consist of a SETTINGS frame.
requirements.why_checkable: The server preface can be parsed and checked for exactly the required frame type.

requirements.quote:
The server connection preface consists of a potentially empty
   SETTINGS frame (Section 6.5) that MUST be the first frame the server
   sends in the HTTP/2 connection.
requirements.condition: When a server begins sending frames on an HTTP/2 connection.
requirements.required_behavior: Send the connection-preface SETTINGS frame as the first frame.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not send any other frame before the connection-preface SETTINGS frame.
requirements.why_checkable: The first server-to-client frame can be captured and checked for type SETTINGS.

requirements.quote:
The server connection preface consists of a potentially empty
   SETTINGS frame (Section 6.5) that MUST be the first frame the server
   sends in the HTTP/2 connection.
requirements.condition: When sending the server connection-preface SETTINGS frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Permit the SETTINGS frame to have an empty payload.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not reject or prevent the server connection preface solely because its SETTINGS payload is empty.
requirements.why_checkable: A zero-length server SETTINGS payload can be generated or received and its handling observed.

requirements.quote:
The SETTINGS frames received from a peer as part of the connection
   preface MUST be acknowledged (see Section 6.5.3) after sending the
   connection preface.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint receives a peer's SETTINGS frame as part of the connection preface.
requirements.required_behavior: Acknowledge the SETTINGS frame after sending the endpoint's own connection preface.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not omit the acknowledgement or send it before the endpoint's own connection preface.
requirements.why_checkable: A bidirectional frame trace can verify both the acknowledgement and its ordering relative to the local connection preface.
